standard_prerequisites.name: Connection time of an endpoint
standard_prerequisites.statement: M(alpha) is the first time the orbit of the left endpoint of the exchanged interval I_alpha meets the set of discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis of the statement bounds the exponent m by it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Conjugacy identities
standard_prerequisites.statement: The reflection conjugates the transformation to its inverse and sends the endpoint of an exchanged interval to the endpoint of the next exchanged interval.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two identities combined in the computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Symmetric interval
standard_prerequisites.statement: A subinterval is symmetric when the reflection of the whole interval maps it to itself by exchanging its endpoints.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property concluded in the second half of the statement.

core_obligations: Apply the generalised conjugacy identity to express the reflection of the m-th backward iterate of an endpoint in terms of the forward iterate of the reflected endpoint (source lines 707-712).
Use the identity describing the reflection of an endpoint of an exchanged interval to identify the reflected index, which is where the index shifted by minus one comes from (source line 712).
Use the bound on the exponent by the connection time to stay away from the discontinuities, so that all the identities invoked are applicable (source lines 713-718).
Conclude that the interval with the two computed endpoints is symmetric for some index, by the criterion that the reflection exchanges its endpoints (source lines 720-724).

proof_roadmap.step: Combine the conjugacy identity for iterates with the reflection of the endpoints.
Use the bound by the connection time to remain at points where the identities are defined.
Read off symmetry of the interval spanned by the two endpoints.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 693-704: for a symmetric interval exchange transformation, an index alpha different from the special one and an exponent m below the connection time, the conjugate of the transformation at the m-th backward iterate of the left endpoint equals the m-th forward iterate of the left endpoint of the previous exchanged interval, and the interval spanned by these two points is symmetric. The proof (source lines 706-724) combines three identities that are not in the statement: the conjugacy identity for iterates, the description of the reflection of an endpoint as the endpoint of the next exchanged interval, and the bound by the connection time, which is what keeps every point involved away from the discontinuities so that the identities may be applied at all. The statement records the resulting formula and the symmetry conclusion only.
